# Daily Nut Intake for an Average Male

## Recommended Amount

Most dietary guidelines (including those from the **American Heart Association** and **FDA**) recommend about:

**1 ounce (28 grams) per day** as a standard serving

This translates to roughly:

| Nut Type | Approximate Count per 1 oz |
|---|---|
| Almonds | ~23 nuts |
| Cashews | ~18 nuts |
| Peanuts | ~28 nuts |
| Pistachios | ~49 kernels |
| Walnuts (halves) | ~14 halves |
| Macadamia | ~10–12 nuts |
| Pecans (halves) | ~19 halves |

## Considerations for Roasted & Salted Specifically

- **Calories**: ~160–200 calories per ounce, so **1–1.5 oz (up to ~42g)** is reasonable within a ~2,500 kcal male diet
- **Sodium**: Salted nuts add ~100–200 mg sodium per ounce. The daily limit is ~2,300 mg, so this matters if salt intake is already high
- **Upper practical limit**: Many nutritionists say up to **2 oz (~56g) per day** is fine, but the salt content of roasted/salted varieties makes sticking closer to **1 oz** wiser

## Bottom Line

An average male can eat roughly **1–1.5 ounces per day**, which is approximately **20–35 nuts** (depending on the type), keeping both calorie and sodium intake in check.
